evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with advanced heart failure and worsening symptoms despite optimal specialist treatment: palliative needs assessment, ICD review, breathlessness and symptom control, and end-of-life planning. Verified against NICE NG106 (palliative care section), NG31 and Saudi MOH Protocol-010.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Opioid dosing for breathlessness specifically — local protocol

pathophysiology.summary: Advanced heart failure is persistent severe symptoms and recurrent decompensation despite optimised therapy. Prognosis is uncertain, so palliative care runs alongside heart failure treatment rather than replacing it.
keyMechanisms: Low cardiac output and congestion cause breathlessness, fatigue, oedema and cachexia.
Renal dysfunction and hypotension limit disease-modifying medicines in late disease.
Implanted defibrillators may deliver distressing shocks near death — review deactivation (NICE NG106).

symptoms: Breathlessness at rest, fatigue, oedema, poor appetite, low mood.
redFlags: Worsening symptoms despite optimal treatment — palliative needs assessment (NICE NG106)
Entering last 2–3 days of life — follow NG31

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Infection, arrhythmia, non-adherence — treat if consistent with goals.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: When symptoms worsen despite optimal specialist treatment
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Unmet physical, psychological, social or spiritual needs.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Discuss with heart failure MDT; involve palliative care skills (NICE NG106 1.12.3–1.12.4). Do not use prognostic tools alone to decide referral.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Discuss deactivation with person and family (NICE NG106).

clinicalManagement.title: Recognise and assess
actions: Palliative needs assessment with the heart failure MDT; access to palliative care skills (NICE NG106).
Advance care planning, including ICD deactivation discussion.

clinicalManagement.title: Symptom control
actions: Continue diuretics for congestion at the lowest effective dose.
Do not offer long-term home oxygen for advanced heart failure (NICE NG106 1.12.1).
Breathlessness: opioid (MOH Protocol-010 morphine starting doses) and non-drug measures (fan, positioning).
Stop medicines no longer providing benefit as death approaches (NICE NG31).

clinicalManagement.title: Last days
actions: Follow NICE NG31 for the last 2–3 days of life (NICE NG106 1.12.5).

learningObjectives: Provide palliative support alongside heart failure treatment for people with advanced disease.
